Numbers are everywhere. They tell the time, the price, the phone number and even the temperature.

The most common numbers are from zero to nine. With these ten digits we can write any number — from one to a billion and more. The Chinese people began to use the ten-digit system more than 3,000 years ago.

Different people like different numbers. In China, eight is a lucky number because it sounds like "getting rich". In the West, seven is lucky because there are seven days in a week and seven colours in a rainbow. But 13 is often seen as unlucky, so many buildings have no 13th floor.

Without numbers, there would be no math, no computers, no smartphones. Learn to love numbers — they make our life easier.

Gunpowder was first used in medicine, then in fireworks, and later in warfare.

These four inventions flew from China to Europe along the Silk Road. They pushed the world into a new age.

Have you ever learned a word in the morning and forgotten it by night? Don't worry — it happens to everyone. The good news is that memory is like a muscle. The more you train it, the stronger it grows.

Here are three simple tricks I use:

1) Repeat with space. I review a new word five minutes later, then one hour, one day, and one week. Each time the word goes deeper into my mind.

2) Make a picture. For the word "elephant", I imagine a pink elephant riding a bicycle. The crazier the picture, the harder it is to forget.

3) Tell a friend. When I explain a rule to my little brother, I understand it twice as well.

My English teacher says, "Your brain is not a warehouse, it is a garden. Water it every day, and the flowers will bloom."

explain: 原文 “memory is like a muscle”。
